editorial:
Imagine waking up in a world where everyone literally walks backward to get where they are going. That is the weird and wild setup you get here. You follow a guy named Minus who is just trying to survive in a cold, corporate office environment. He is fighting his own natural urges to move forward because in this society, doing that makes you an outcast. It feels like a strange dream, but it quickly turns into a story about how hard it is to fit in when you are different from everyone else. The vibe is a mix of a workplace comedy and a strange social experiment that keeps you wondering why things are this way.

The acting is surprisingly good, and the way the actors move makes the whole concept feel real instead of just silly. Some parts move a bit slow, but the tension builds up nicely as Minus tries to climb the company ladder without getting caught. If you want something totally different for movie night, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the end, Minus finally stops pretending and decides to walk forward in public. This act of rebellion inspires a few other coworkers to stop following the weird rules too. The big twist is that the corporate leaders only forced the backward walking to keep people confused and easy to control. By the final scene, the social order breaks down, and Minus finds true freedom by simply facing the right direction.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about rebels and strange alternate worlds.
